items.claim: The front seam at Isa.51.20|Isa.51.21 is argued from an imperative onset the bytes do not carry verse-initially, the span's rare cup-of-wrath vocabulary that binds it back into the preceding recital is undisclosed, and the paragraph mark recruited as onset corroboration in fact divides the span internally.
items.evidence: Onset: the verse-initial token at oshb:Isa.51.21 is לָכֵ֛ן, a consequential connector standing before the imperative, spliced as לָכֵ֛ן שִׁמְעִי (oshb:Isa.51.21, byte); verse-initial occurrences of that connector are attested at 20 verses in this book (skeleton-tier sweep: 20 verses), so the byte-initial form resumes the wrath recital rather than opening unprefaced, and the rationale's 'a fresh imperative summons opens this span' overstates what stands first. Cross-seam cohesion: the frame verse inside the span reuses the preceding unit's cup construction — קֻבַּ֨עַת֙ כּ֣וֹס (oshb:Isa.51.22, byte) against קֻבַּ֜עַת כּ֧וֹס (oshb:Isa.51.17, byte); the two sites match each other at accent_stripped tier, never byte. Each of the three cup-of-wrath tokens — the cup noun כּ֣וֹס (oshb:Isa.51.22, byte) and the goblet noun קֻבַּ֨עַת֙ (oshb:Isa.51.22, byte) and the reeling noun הַתַּרְעֵלָ֑ה (oshb:Isa.51.22, byte) — is attested in exactly two verses in the whole book (skeleton-tier sweep: 2 verses each, MT 51:17 and MT 51:22), and oshb:Isa.51.22 inverts the earlier order, giving cup-plus-reeling first and goblet-plus-cup-of-my-wrath second. A byte-true device this rare straddling the row's own front seam argues continuity with the preceding recital unless disclosed; the rejected alternative names that recital but rests its refusal solely on the overstated onset claim. Mark reading: the setumah recruited as onset corroboration is keyed to MT 51:21, but the seg stands after that verse's end-of-verse punctuation, so it divides MT 51:21 from MT 51:22 inside the span, and the span's actual front seam MT 51:20|51:21 carries no mark at all. The same layer is read as closing after its keyed verse at MT 51:23, 52:2, 52:10 and 52:12 in this cluster's other rationales, so the onset reading here is both inconsistent and span-internal (tier-3, single witness; absence is never counterevidence). Verified sound and not challenged: all three pointed splices reach byte tier at their cited verses, the frame at oshb:Isa.51.22 is divine and its suffixed lordship title stands in the quoted bytes, and the closing setumah at MT 51:23 is correctly read.

items.claim: The row's recurrence evidence is mis-tiered — the doubled awake-imperative here is not byte-identical to the earlier one it is said to match exactly — and the stem label attached to the intervening awake-summons is asserted with no quoted form.
items.evidence: Mis-tiered recurrence: עוּרִ֥י עוּרִ֛י (oshb:Isa.52.1, byte at its own site) against עוּרִ֨י עוּרִ֤י (oshb:Isa.51.9, byte at its own site). The accent bytes differ on both members of the pair, and checking either run against the other verse reaches accent_stripped tier only, never byte. The rationale's 'byte-matching that earlier shape' and the device note's 'matching the byte shape at web:Isa.51.9 exactly' are therefore false at the tier claimed; the honest recurrence tier is accent_stripped, which under the campaign's tier-disclosure standard still carries the cohesion argument but must be named as such. Unquoted form-class label: the device note calls MT 51:17 'the Hitpael shape' with no splice; the bytes there read הִתְעוֹרְרִ֣י הִֽתְעוֹרְרִ֗י (oshb:Isa.51.17, byte) — a reduplicated hollow-root pattern, not the simple reflexive stem the label names. No morphology layer is staged to settle stem class, so the label should be held rather than asserted, and a Hebrew claim about a verse outside the span owes a quoted form. Undigited ordinal: 'the third member of the awake-imperative series' blends two lexemes without a count. The doubled onset of oshb:Isa.52.1's verb is attested at exactly 2 verses (skeleton-tier sweep: 2 verses, MT 51:9 and MT 52:1); the doubled onset of oshb:Isa.51.17's verb at exactly 1 verse (skeleton-tier sweep: 1 verse, MT 51:17). Disclosure gap: a paseq seg stands at MT 52:1 inside this span (count-only, single witness; intra-verse position is unsourceable) and is not disclosed while the row engages the ketiv/qere and parashah layers in the same span. Verified sound and not challenged: the ketiv/qere note at MT 52:2 is real and disclosed, the ketiv and qere tokens both stand inside the quoted byte-tier run, and the setumah marks at MT 51:23 and MT 52:2 are real and correctly read as closing after their keyed verses.

items.claim: The one-verse cut is tested only against the seam behind it while a two-verse-rare catchword and a shared frame-onset construction carry the verse across its own rear seam undisclosed.
items.evidence: Cross-seam catchword: חִנָּ֖ם (oshb:Isa.52.3, byte) recurs as חִנָּ֑ם (oshb:Isa.52.5, byte), the two sites matching each other at accent_stripped tier, and the token is attested in exactly two verses in the whole book (skeleton-tier sweep: 2 verses, MT 52:3 and MT 52:5). The sold-for-nothing / taken-for-nothing pair runs straight across this span's rear seam into the second verse of the following unit, which argues MT 52:3-52:6 as one movement unless disclosed. Nothing in the row names it, and the rejected alternative tests only the seam behind the verse (folding back into the awake-Zion imperatives), leaving the seam that the byte evidence actually contests untested — at the finest granularity available, a single-verse unit. Shared onset shape: the frames on either side of that rear seam share their construction, not merely their function — כִּֽי כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר (oshb:Isa.52.3, byte) and כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ (oshb:Isa.52.4, byte), conjunction plus messenger formula in both, matching each other at skeleton tier. 'A further messenger formula, separately worded' understates a repeated onset construction. Verified sound and not challenged: the pointed splice reaches byte tier at its cited verse, the frame is divine and names the deity in its own bytes, the setumah at MT 52:2 is real and correctly read as closing before the onset, and no ketiv/qere note falls in this span.

items.claim: The span's frame ownership, its ketiv/qere and parashah disclosures, its absence claim and its internal cohesion all hold in the bytes.
items.evidence: Frame: כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה (oshb:Isa.52.4, byte) is a divine messenger frame with the lordship title standing in the quoted bytes, and the two postpositive divine-speech signatures inside MT 52:5 — נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.52.5, byte), occurring twice in that verse — are internal signatures rather than fresh onsets, which is exactly how the row holds them. Ketiv/qere: MT 52:5 really does carry two variant notes, the ketiv and qere tokens of both pairs stand inside the byte-tier splice, and the row discloses the doubling without adjudicating either reading; no note falls at MT 52:4 or MT 52:6, so nothing further is owed in the span. Parashah: the span's absence claim is true — no petuchah and no setumah is recorded from MT 52:3 through MT 52:7, the nearest marks standing at MT 52:2 and MT 52:10 (tier-3, single witness; absence is never counterevidence). Internal cohesion supporting the three-verse hold: שְׁמִ֥י (oshb:Isa.52.5, byte) and שְׁמִ֑י (oshb:Isa.52.6, byte) chain the name motif across the span's interior, and the closing self-identification the row names does stand in the Hebrew — הַה֔וּא כִּֽי אֲנִי ה֥וּא (oshb:Isa.52.6, byte). Open items, none boundary-affecting: the two-verse-rare for-nothing catchword shared with the preceding verse (MT 52:3, MT 52:5; skeleton-tier sweep: 2 verses) crosses this span's front seam and is not named, though the row does test that seam as its rival; the ketiv/qere apparatus is cited under a web: prefix in the device note although that layer is Masoretic-keyed, which is harmless only because chapter 52 is identity-numbered in both witnesses; and the English run quoted for MT 52:6 is the verse's last clause only, while the formula it names sits in the Hebrew splice.

items.claim: The span's unit label rests entirely on the one verse the row never engages in the bytes, and the English run standing in for that verse is not the translation's wording.
items.evidence: Unengaged driver verse: the doxological label is carried by the sung imperatives at MT 52:9 — פִּצְח֤וּ רַנְּנוּ֙ (oshb:Isa.52.9, byte) — and MT 52:9 is the only verse of this span with no pointed splice anywhere in the row. The three verses that are spliced (MT 52:7, 52:8, 52:10) are exclamation, report and announcement rather than sung imperative, so the label's actual byte warrant goes unstated while an unquoted verse carries it. Quote fidelity: the device note's English run for that verse, set in straight quotes as 'break out into joy, sing together', is not the translation's wording at web:Isa.52.9, which reads “Break out into joy! Sing together, you waste places of Jerusalem;”. Straight quoting keeps a non-verbatim run of translation text inside a field that carries that verse's own web: ref out of reach of the verbatim arm; the convention reserves curly quotes for translation text precisely so that such runs are checked. Unsupported characterisation: calling MT 52:9 both the 'structural center' of the span and a match to a 'recognized hymn-closure pattern' is self-contradictory and carries no evidence of either. Verified sound and not challenged: the onset מַה נָּאו֨וּ (oshb:Isa.52.7, byte) is exclamatory, the following unit opens on a doubled imperative, the setumah at MT 52:10 is real and correctly read as closing after its keyed verse, and no ketiv/qere note falls in the span. Undisclosed but favourable to the hold: the herald participle at MT 52:7 is attested in exactly 2 verses (skeleton-tier sweep: 2 verses, MT 41:27 and MT 52:7), and זְר֣וֹעַ קָדְשׁ֔וֹ (oshb:Isa.52.10, byte) belongs to an arm-token attested in exactly 4 verses (skeleton-tier sweep: 4 verses, MT 51:9, 52:10, 53:1, 63:12).

items.claim: The rear seam is asserted from workflow position and from a structural fact the row's own parent field contradicts, with no byte evidence offered at that seam, while the row carries high confidence.
items.evidence: False structural claim: the rationale calls the seam at MT 52:12|52:13 'the frame boundary this campaign has fixed at the parent-collection line', but this row and the row that follows both carry the identical parent frame string spanning Isa.49.1-Isa.55.13, so that seam is not a parent line; the parent lines nearest to it are Isa.48.22|Isa.49.1 and Isa.55.13|Isa.56.1. As written the claim asserts an architectural authority the row's own field denies. Vacuous rival: the rejected alternative sets the extension aside 'because this row's own assigned range ends at web:Isa.52.12' — a workflow reason, not a textual one — and the device note repeats the same process framing. The one field designed to test the cut therefore carries no evidence at all, and confidence is nonetheless recorded as high; the only signal actually supplied at that seam is the setumah at MT 52:12, which is tier-3, single-witness, and never a driver. Available and unused byte evidence: the next verse opens הִנֵּ֥ה יַשְׂכִּ֖יל עַבְדִּ֑י (oshb:Isa.52.13, byte), a presentative onset carrying a first-person-suffixed servant designation and a third-person verb, against this span's second-person-plural departure imperatives ס֤וּרוּ ס֨וּרוּ֙ צְא֣וּ מִשָּׁ֔ם (oshb:Isa.52.11, byte) and its escort promise הֹלֵ֤ךְ לִפְנֵיכֶם֙ יְהוָ֔ה וּמְאַסִּפְכֶ֖ם אֱלֹהֵ֥י (oshb:Isa.52.12, byte). A one-sentence byte argument was there to be made and none was. Verified sound and not challenged: the doubled onset imperative at oshb:Isa.52.11 reaches byte tier, the setumah marks at MT 52:10 and MT 52:12 are real and correctly read as closing after their keyed verses, and no ketiv/qere note falls in the span.

items.claim: The rear seam is argued from a person-shift visible only in the translation, the same criterion cuts inside the span undisclosed, and two byte-true hooks cross that seam without mention.
items.evidence: Translation-carried seam argument: the close is argued from a shift to a communal first-person-plural voice at the next verse, but no pointed form is quoted at MT 52:15 or at MT 53:1 anywhere in the row — the discriminator rides entirely on the English rendering. In the bytes the shift is real (לִשְׁמֻעָתֵ֑נוּ, oshb:Isa.53.1, byte) but the same verse hooks back across the seam: שָׁמְע֖וּ (oshb:Isa.52.15, byte) and לִשְׁמֻעָתֵ֑נוּ share the hearing root at skeleton tier, and וּזְר֥וֹעַ יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Isa.53.1, byte) resumes זְר֣וֹעַ קָדְשׁ֔וֹ (oshb:Isa.52.10, byte) — an arm-token attested in exactly 4 verses in the whole book (skeleton-tier sweep: 4 verses, MT 51:9, 52:10, 53:1, 63:12). Byte-true devices straddling the row's own rear seam argue continuity unless disclosed, and neither is named. The criterion is not applied inside the span: MT 52:13 speaks of the figure in the third person (יַשְׂכִּ֖יל עַבְדִּ֑י יָר֧וּם, oshb:Isa.52.13, byte), MT 52:14 addresses him in the second person masculine singular (כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר שָׁמְמ֤וּ עָלֶ֨יךָ֙ רַבִּ֔ים, oshb:Isa.52.14, byte), and MT 52:15 returns to the third (עָלָ֛יו, oshb:Isa.52.15, byte). The rationale calls MT 52:14-15 one continuous astonished-nations description and never names that internal shift, which is sharper than the one used to argue the close. Internal contradiction and label: the onset הִנֵּ֥ה יַשְׂכִּ֖יל עַבְדִּ֑י (oshb:Isa.52.13, byte) is called a 'divine first-person oracle-opening formula' in the rationale while the rejected alternative concedes that no explicit frame formula marks a fresh oracle boundary here. The presentative particle is not one of this book's frame formulas, and the verb is third-person — only the suffix on the servant noun is first-person. The same servant noun is then filed under a divine-title signal class, which misassigns it: it is the servant designation with a first-person suffix, not a title of the deity, and this book's divine-title objects are a different set. Verified sound and not challenged: the single pointed splice reaches byte tier at its cited verse, the setumah at MT 52:12 is real and correctly typed and read as closing before the onset (though cited under a web: prefix while that layer is Masoretic-keyed), no ketiv/qere note falls in MT 52:13-52:15, no messenger or narrator frame interrupts the span, and the referent is properly left undecided.
